summary: Tom De Rauw works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Ann Heirman and holds an AAP post at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Tom Ginsburg (born 1968) specializes in Buddhist studies and law. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1985–1999), taught at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2000–2008), and joined the University of Chicago around 2008.

Tom Hannes is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a bachelor's at the University of Antwerp (1988–1991), a master's at KU Leuven (1991–1993), and worked as a postdoctoral researcher at Eindhoven University of Technology in 2020.

Tom Tillemans (born 1950) is a philosopher, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctorate under Jacques May. He succeeded May (1992–2011), became Emeritus Professor at the University of Lausanne, and was Visiting Numata Chair at Calgary (~2013).
Tomohiro Manabe specializes in Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2020) and as an associate professor at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

Tomoko Masuzawa specializes in religious studies and history. She studied at International Christian University, Yale University (MA ~1977–1979), and UC Santa Barbara (PhD ~1979–1985). She held faculty posts at UNC Chapel Hill (~1986–2000) and the University of Michigan (1999).
Tomomichi Nitta works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held an appointment as a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012) and as a professor at Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Tomoyasu Oshima specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Toshifumi Goto (attested 2012) and served as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2012).
Tomoyuki Komine (born 1971) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University, where he later worked as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).
Tomoyuki Uno is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He was a JSPS special researcher (attested 1998) and served as an assistant professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

Tomy Augustine works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under C. S. Sundaram at the University of Madras and earned a PhD at Banaras Hindu University under Munni K. Agrawal. He held a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

Toni Huber works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Jim Wilson, Paul Harrison, and William Sax, earning a PhD from the University of Canterbury (-1993). He held professorships at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 2000) and Humboldt University (attested 2006–2009).

Toni Schmid (1897–1972) was a Tibetologist and historian. She earned doctorates at the University of Vienna (~1916–1922) and Lund University (1925–1931), studied under Helmer Smith, and served as antiquarian at the Royal Swedish Academy of Letters, History and Antiquities (1944–1968).

Tony K. Stewart (born 1954) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976). He served as professor at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and held a post at Vanderbilt University (~2011).

Tony Walter (born 1948) works in religious studies. After studies at Durham and the University of Aberdeen (PhD 1970–1975), he held posts at Aberdeen (1970–1974), the University of Reading (1994–2006), and the University of Bath (professor from 2006, emeritus 2015).

Torakazu Doi (1902–1971) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe (~1922–1925). He held posts at Sagami Women's University and Dokkyo University (~1964–1971).

Torkel Brekke (born 1970) studied at the University of Oslo and earned a DPhil at Oxford (1996–1999) under Richard Gombrich. He held positions at Oslo (~2001–2019), PRIO (2016–2020), Oslo Metropolitan University (2019–2023), and MF Norwegian School of Theology (2023).

Toru Funayama (born 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner (1991–1992). He held faculty posts at Kyushu University (attested 1999–2003) and Kyoto University (attested 1995–2019).

Toru Haneda (1882–1955) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Sinological history. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (doctorate 1922), he spent decades as lecturer, professor, and director at Kyoto University, later chairing the Toho Gakkai (1947).

Toru Kumeji specializes in Buddhist studies and computational humanities. He has held positions at the Center for Open Humanities Data and as a chief researcher at the Humanities Information Studies Institute (attested 2015).
